sections.h2: What is the Danville housing market like for someone who needs to sell?
sections.html:
Danville is an affordable, slower-moving market where repair costs can rival a house's value. The Census Bureau reports a median value of $79,000 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024, compared with $334,100 in Chicago and $311,400 in Crystal Lake.

The city is the seat of Vermilion County, and the Census Bureau estimated its population at 28,138 on July 1, 2025, down 3.6 percent from the April 2020 base of 29,200. It had 33,027 residents in 2010. Owner-occupied homes make up 57.3 percent of housing, median gross rent is $846, and there are 11,901 households of about 2.19 people. Median household income is $45,957, 24.5 percent of residents are in poverty and 19.4 percent are 65 or older.

Those figures explain why many Danville sellers are heirs, landlords with aging rentals, or owners of houses that have sat empty. When a roof or furnace costs a large share of what the house would sell for, an as-is sale deserves a serious look next to a listing.

sections.h2: How does Danville's vacant building ordinance affect a sale?
sections.html:
If the house is empty, Danville's Chapter 169 can add registration fees that must be settled before the house changes hands. The ordinance, posted on the city's website, says the owner of a vacant building must register with the Public Development Department within 30 days after the building becomes vacant.

Danville vacant building rules that matter at closing
RuleWhat the ordinance says
Who must registerThe owner, within 30 days after the building becomes vacant
Residential registration fee$50 (non-residential is $100)
Annual fee if the building stays vacant$500, held in abeyance while permitted repairs make progress
Fees at transferPaid by the owner before any transfer, and disclosed by the seller to the buyer
If unpaid at transferNew owner pays the annual fee plus $300 within 30 days
Penalty for violations$250 to $2,500 per offense, with each day counted separately

A new owner must also re-register a vacant building within 30 days of any transfer and follow the plan the previous owner filed until changes are approved. A building counts as vacant when it is unoccupied and, for example, unsecured, unsafe, under an order to correct violations or illegally occupied. Ask the city's Public Development Department whether your property is on the registry before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What other Danville city rules should a seller check?
sections.html:
Utility accounts and code enforcement are the two other places the city touches a sale. The city's utility billing office is at 17 W Main Street, and its FAQ says to bring a signed and dated copy of the deed so the account can be prorated, because accounts are billed by date of ownership, not occupancy.

  • Account name: residential accounts must be in the owner's name, and a landlord's bill stays in the landlord's name.
  • Flat fees: city ordinances require every property owner to pay flat sewer and solid waste fees regardless of usage, so a vacant house still gets a bill.
  • Due dates: accounts beginning with 08 are due on the 8th of each month and those beginning with 04 on the 20th, adjusted when the date falls on a weekend.
  • Rental registration: the city's environmental code program says all rental units and vacant structures must be registered and a fee paid each year.

Common code violations the program lists include grass over six inches, trash in the yard, inoperable vehicles, missing house numbers and toters left out too long. Clearing those cheaply before showings makes the house look cared for and avoids a notice during the sale.

sections.h2: Where are Danville deeds recorded and what does the filing involve?
sections.html:
Deeds for Danville property go to the Vermilion County Recorder at 201 N Vermilion Street, Danville, Illinois 61832. The office phone is (217) 554-6040, and it accepts documents by mail if you include a check for the exact fee and a self-addressed return envelope.

The Recorder's FAQ explains the key rule: every sale or gift needs a newly prepared, signed, notarized and recorded deed. When the sale involves consideration above $100, Illinois Form PTAX-203 must be completed and submitted with the deed. The form collects the state and county transfer taxes, which are based on the sale price. A gift is exempt from those taxes, but the deed must carry the right exemption statement. The state rate, set in 35 ILCS 200/31-10, is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500.

The Recorder does not give legal advice, does not run title searches and cannot refer you to an attorney. A copy of a recorded deed costs $1.00 per page, and the office says its goal is to return a deed presented in person right after scanning, usually within five minutes. For current recording fees, call the office, because the schedule is revised from time to time. Questions about back taxes go to the County Treasurer, and parcel details to the Supervisor of Assessments.

sections.h2: What is the layout and history of Danville that buyers care about?
sections.html:
Danville was founded in 1827 and sits on the Vermilion River about 120 miles south of Chicago, 35 miles east of Champaign-Urbana and 90 miles west of Indianapolis. Illinois Route 1, U.S. Route 136 and U.S. Route 150 meet in the city, and Interstate 74 passes through the south end of town. Lake Vermilion, a 1,000-acre reservoir, lies on the northwest side.

The city is made up of many neighborhoods. Fourteen have or have had neighborhood associations and nine have official borders. West Downtown dates to the later 19th century, and Lincoln Park is a locally designated historic district with a 22-acre park and the Lamon House. Wikipedia describes three broad districts: downtown, the retail district along the north side corridor, and the campus district that holds Danville Area Community College and the VA campuses on the east side.

Abraham Lincoln practiced law here for about 18 years on the 8th Judicial Circuit, and the city counts over 12 sites commemorating that history. The Village Mall opened in 1975, retail spread north along Route 1 after the early 1990s, and parts of the city fall within an Illinois Enterprise Zone and five Tax Increment Financing districts. Mean travel time to work is 14.4 minutes by Census figures, far lower than Chicago's 33.1.

sections.h2: Which schools and amenities should be mentioned when you sell a Danville house?
sections.html:
Most of Danville lies in Danville Community Consolidated School District 118, and a small piece extends into the Bismarck-Henning Consolidated Unit School District. Danville High School and Danville New Tech High are public options, and private schools include Schlarman Academy, Danville Christian Academy and Trinity Lutheran School.

Recreation is a selling point. The city maintains more than 20 parks and recreation facilities, and Wikipedia reports that county parks, three state parks and city parkland together exceed 15,000 acres. Lake Vermilion allows fishing and boating, and the Heron County Park Wetlands Boardwalk extends into the lake. Danville Mass Transit runs 14 fixed bus routes, and the Vermilion Regional Airport serves general aviation.

When you write or discuss the listing, lead with what the price figures cannot show: a short commute, a lake, a historic district and a community college campus.

sections.h2: How should a Danville owner compare a cash buyer with listing the house?
sections.html:
Set the numbers side by side and include the costs that never appear in an offer. A house valued near the city median of $79,000 can leave little room for repairs, agent fees and months of carrying costs, so a quick as-is closing can be worth more than it first appears.

  • Get written repair bids for the roof, furnace, plumbing and electrical items an inspector would flag.
  • Check whether the building is registered as vacant and whether any fees are owed.
  • Ask for the closing date and confirm who pays recording and title charges.
  • Compare the figure against a listing agent's price opinion for the same house.

Illinois law requires you to deliver a residential disclosure report before the contract is signed under 765 ILCS 77/20, even when you sell as-is. If the house came to you from an estate, ask an attorney whether title is clear before accepting any offer.

faqs.q: Can I sell a vacant house in Danville?
faqs.a: Yes. If the house is registered as vacant, the city ordinance requires the fees to be paid before transfer and disclosed to the buyer. An unpaid annual fee passes to the new owner with an extra $300.

faqs.q: Where do I record the deed for a Danville sale?
faqs.a: Take or mail it to the Vermilion County Recorder at 201 N Vermilion Street in Danville. A sale above $100 also needs Illinois Form PTAX-203 filed with the deed.

faqs.q: How do I transfer utilities when my Danville house sells?
faqs.a: Bring a signed and dated copy of the deed to the city's utility billing office at 17 W Main Street or email it. The city prorates the account by date of ownership.

faqs.q: Do I owe a transfer tax to the city of Danville?
faqs.a: The Recorder's page describes state and county transfer taxes collected through the PTAX-203 form and does not list a separate city tax. Ask the title company to confirm the charges that apply to your sale.

faqs.q: Do I have to register my Danville rental before selling it?
faqs.a: The city's code enforcement program says rental units must be registered and a fee paid each year. Contact the code enforcement office to confirm the registration is current before you sell.
